title: SQL Injection in Python
description: A Flask endpoint builds a SQL query with string interpolation, letting an attacker alter the query structure.
secure_code:
import sqlite3

app = None  # Flask app defined elsewhere, see pattern below

def get_user(username):
    conn = sqlite3.connect("users.db")
    cur = conn.cursor()
    # GOOD: use placeholders so the driver treats input as data, not SQL
    query = "SELECT * FROM users WHERE username = ?"
    cur.execute(query, (username,))
    return cur.fetchall()

# ---- Flask example using a parameterized call ----
from flask import Flask, request, jsonify

app = Flask(__name__)

@app.route("/user")
def user():
    name = request.args.get("name", "")
    rows = get_user(name)
    return jsonify({"rows": rows})

finding.title: SQL Injection
finding.description: Untrusted user input is concatenated directly into a SQL statement, so an attacker can inject SQL parts like ' OR '1'='1'.
finding.why_dangerous: The database parses user-controlled text as executable query code, not as data.
finding.impact: Unauthorized database access, data theft, deletion, or privilege escalation.
finding.fix: Bind input with placeholders (?) and pass values as arguments so the driver escapes them as data.
learning_example: Attacker input: ' OR '1'='1 => selects every row
The same input passed as a parameter is just a harmless string of characters

checklist: Validate and sanitize all user input before use
Use parameterized statements or prepared queries
Apply least privilege to the database account
Review all dynamic SQL for interpolation
Enable SQL error hiding to avoid leaking schema detail
